integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action, cinematic, a steady forward tracking shot follows a young man walking briskly through the grand exhibition halls and display cases of a natural history museum, weaving between the cases. Warm evening sunlight slants down from the towering glass ceiling above, carving distinct bands of brightness through the space, with tiny particles drifting slowly in the light; the atmosphere is quiet and solemn. A sharp system alert tone abruptly shatters the calm. The man stops short at once, his expression darkening, his brow tightening, wariness and impatience flashing across his eyes. [Shot 2] At 00:05.000, the camera shifts into a 360-degree circular slow-motion orbit as his expression turns cold and hard and he suddenly raises one hand. A perceptible transparent shockwave ripples outward from him as the center, and at that exact instant all ambient sound is completely stripped away, the alert tone cutting off abruptly. The orbit reveals the eerie, surreal stillness: a visitor's astonished face frozen mid-reaction, an artifact slipping from the edge of a display stand hanging motionless in midair, and a flock of pigeons outside the glass curtain wall suspended with wings half-spread, everything fallen into absolute stillness. [Shot 3] At 00:10.000, the circling camera settles into a medium close-up from the front of the man, the only being still able to move in this halted space. His face carries heavy resolve intertwined with barely concealed exhaustion. He slowly lowers his arm, his breathing slightly hurried. Behind him, rows of warm yellow pendant lights in the lounge exhibition area cast soft background illumination, yet within the absolute silence that warmth feels oddly oppressive, making the outline of his solitary figure stand out starkly.

overall_soundscape: Quiet museum ambience with soft footsteps and drifting room tone, abruptly pierced by a sharp system alert tone. At the shockwave moment every ambient sound is stripped away into total silence, and only a faint low-frequency hum remains afterward, flickering in and out.
